Develop and monitor individualized housing and service plans.

Job Summary

Pacific Clinics is providing Crisis Response Team services for Nevada County which will include the provisions of emergency crisis intervention services to Nevada County residents. They will be provided 24 hours a day, 7 days a week and 365 days per year. Services will include both community-based mobile crisis services and responses to emergency departments. The Crisis Response Team will intervene to de-escalate the behavioral health crisis, including those who are acutely suicidal, homicidal or gravely disabled and stabilize the client at their location, reducing the need for higher level of care.

Pacific Clinics is seeking a dedicated Crisis Clinical Program Manager to implement and lead our Mobile Crisis Response Team in Nevada County. This role calls for a leader with passion and expertise in serving those in the community with complex needs, and who is excited about partnering with the crisis continuum of care in Nevada County. We’re looking for someone with strong clinical knowledge, crisis experience, and team oriented who is ready to build and develop programming to positively impact the residents of Nevada County.

Clients remain in the program for as long as they require subsidized housing. For many individuals this may mean their entire lifetime.

Position Description:  

Silver Lining Mentoring (SLM) is seeking a collaborative, systems-oriented Program Manager to lead our e-Mentoring program. This person will manage the day-to-day operations and program quality of SLM's e-Mentoring program, and will play a key role in identifying challenges and problem-solving as the program grows and scales by building out the policies, procedures, and tools needed to support that growth.

This position reports to the Senior Director of Programs and works within the Programs Department alongside SLM's other Program Managers, the Volunteer Manager, and the Enrollment Specialist especially for mentee and mentor recruitment efforts. Success in this role requires flexibility and strong collaboration skills, as the Program Manager will partner closely with this team and other departments to balance program needs with organizational goals.

This role is designed for growth. It will start by managing a caseload of e-matches directly, but this is not a permanent caseload-management position: as the program expands over the next 6–12 months, direct reports will be added and this role will transition into supervising the staff who provide match support. Because of that trajectory, prior people management, sound judgment around participant safety, harm reduction, and organizational liability is essential from day one. 

The ideal candidate will bring attention to detail and competency in program development to ensure a smooth and efficient youth and volunteer experience that upholds Silver Lining Mentoring policies, procedures, values, and approach, along with a genuine interest in building and improving systems — not just running an existing playbook. Experience related to youth development, the foster care system, and/or young adult mentoring is valued, and experience maintaining a digital communications or virtual engagement platform is highly desirable.

Responsibilities:

Program Management, Infrastructure & Quality (40%)

Platform Management
: Manage the e-mentoring platform(s), including day-to-day support needs and community or communication features, in collaboration with the platform provider.
Volunteer Screening, Training & Engagement
: Partner with Enrollment Team members to screen and train prospective e-mentors, and lead ongoing engagement of approved-but-unmatched mentors to keep them informed and ready to match.
Adaptive Problem-Solving & Continuous Improvement
: Serve as the primary problem-solver for new or unanticipated challenges that arise as a new program, proposing and implementing practical solutions and escalating larger issues as needed. Recommend and implement process improvements to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the e-mentoring program as it evolves.
Policies & Procedures
: Build out and maintain policy and procedure manuals for the e-mentoring program, ensuring program delivery is consistent with SLM’s best practices, values, and the Elements of Effective Practice for Mentoring.
Systems & Tools
: Develop and refine Salesforce, Jotform, DocuSign, and other tools/workflows to support e-match tracking, enrollment paperwork, reporting, and data management
Progress Tracking & Data Management
: Monitor program progress against key performance indicators (KPIs) and assist the Senior Director of Programs in preparing status updates for organizational leadership. Additionally, maintain accurate program and match data in Salesforce, applying SLM's data safety and confidentiality standards, and support the evaluation of that data to inform program improvements.
Evaluation Administration
: Administer the program's evaluation instruments, including survey distribution, response tracking, follow-up with non-respondents, and timely data entry, to ensure complete and usable evaluation data.

Caseload & Match Management (35%)

Match Support
: Manage a caseload of e-matches, providing regular, personalized support to mentors and mentees to help each relationship thrive virtually. This includes conducting regular check-ins with matches to monitor relationship health, celebrate milestones, and identify and address concerns early and guiding matches through intentional match closure/graduation. 
Harm Reduction & Adult-Centered Support
: Provide match support grounded in harm reduction and trauma-informed practice, centering autonomy, informed decision-making, and self-determination given that most e-mentees are legal adults.
Risk Management
: Identify potential risks or liabilities specific to the virtual nature of matches and respond according to SLM policy, escalating to the Senior Director of Programs as needed.
Mentee Engagement Innovation
: Design and implement creative strategies to sustain mentee engagement, including quarterly workshops, compelling rollouts of new resources and opportunities, and persistent, creative follow-up with unresponsive or low-engagement mentees.
Caseload Calibration
: Partner with the Senior Director of Programs to to establish a pathway toward supervising future match support roles in e-mentoring (e.g., track workload and help determine sustainable caseload sizes as the program grows, provide insights for hiring/onboarding new e-mentoring staff, etc.) 

Collaboration & Program Support (25%)

Partnership Support
: Support the identification and maintenance of relationships with strategic partners relevant to the e-mentoring program, in coordination with the Senior Director of Programs and Chief Strategy Officer.
Team Collaboration
: Participate as an active member of the Programs Department, sharing updates and collaborating with other Program Managers on shared practices, tools, and challenges; coordinate with the Volunteer Manager and Enrollment Specialist on mentor recruitment/allocation and mentee recruitment and enrollment specific to e-mentoring.
Cross-Departmental Collaboration
: Participate in relevant working groups to promote cross-departmental collaboration and strategy insight on programming that impacts mentees, mentors, and program staff, including partnering with the Development team to identify and uplift match experiences and stories.
Partner & Donor Reporting
: Compile program reports for partners and donors, pulling and interpreting Salesforce data to present the right metrics, and proactively flagging reportable milestones and trends to the Senior Director of Programs and Development team.
DEI Engagement
: Actively engage in SLM's Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) efforts, such as attending all-staff trainings, providing and receiving feedback, and embracing accountability.
Professionalism & Confidentiality
: Maintain the professional competence and confidentiality necessary to perform job responsibilities.

Qualifications:

Our ideal candidate will be a values-led, adaptable individual interested in supporting youth impacted by
foster care. Data shows that BIPOC and women often rule themselves out from job opportunities when
they don’t feel they fit 100% of the criteria listed in a job description. If that sounds like you, don’t rule
yourself out.

Sound judgment, especially around participant safety, harm reduction, and organizational liability. This role is expected to grow into a supervisory position over the next 6–12 months, so the ability to make and stand behind good calls independently, and to know when and how to escalate is essential

Lead end-to-end technical program management of the First Mile non-POR REI portfolio, including business requirements, technical design reviews, approvals, CARs, and stakeholder communication through BRs and flashes.

Position Description:  

Silver Lining Mentoring (SLM) is seeking a collaborative, systems-oriented Program Manager to lead our e-Mentoring program. This person will manage the day-to-day operations and program quality of SLM's e-Mentoring program, and will play a key role in identifying challenges and problem-solving as the program grows and scales by building out the policies, procedures, and tools needed to support that growth.

This position reports to the Senior Director of Programs and works within the Programs Department alongside SLM's other Program Managers, the Volunteer Manager, and the Enrollment Specialist especially for mentee and mentor recruitment efforts. Success in this role requires flexibility and strong collaboration skills, as the Program Manager will partner closely with this team and other departments to balance program needs with organizational goals.

This role is designed for growth. It will start by managing a caseload of e-matches directly, but this is not a permanent caseload-management position: as the program expands over the next 6–12 months, direct reports will be added and this role will transition into supervising the staff who provide match support. Because of that trajectory, prior people management, sound judgment around participant safety, harm reduction, and organizational liability is essential from day one. 

The ideal candidate will bring attention to detail and competency in program development to ensure a smooth and efficient youth and volunteer experience that upholds Silver Lining Mentoring policies, procedures, values, and approach, along with a genuine interest in building and improving systems — not just running an existing playbook. Experience related to youth development, the foster care system, and/or young adult mentoring is valued, and experience maintaining a digital communications or virtual engagement platform is highly desirable.

Responsibilities:

Program Management, Infrastructure & Quality (40%)

Platform Management
: Manage the e-mentoring platform(s), including day-to-day support needs and community or communication features, in collaboration with the platform provider.
Volunteer Screening, Training & Engagement
: Partner with Enrollment Team members to screen and train prospective e-mentors, and lead ongoing engagement of approved-but-unmatched mentors to keep them informed and ready to match.
Adaptive Problem-Solving & Continuous Improvement
: Serve as the primary problem-solver for new or unanticipated challenges that arise as a new program, proposing and implementing practical solutions and escalating larger issues as needed. Recommend and implement process improvements to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the e-mentoring program as it evolves.
Policies & Procedures
: Build out and maintain policy and procedure manuals for the e-mentoring program, ensuring program delivery is consistent with SLM’s best practices, values, and the Elements of Effective Practice for Mentoring.
Systems & Tools
: Develop and refine Salesforce, Jotform, DocuSign, and other tools/workflows to support e-match tracking, enrollment paperwork, reporting, and data management
Progress Tracking & Data Management
: Monitor program progress against key performance indicators (KPIs) and assist the Senior Director of Programs in preparing status updates for organizational leadership. Additionally, maintain accurate program and match data in Salesforce, applying SLM's data safety and confidentiality standards, and support the evaluation of that data to inform program improvements.
Evaluation Administration
: Administer the program's evaluation instruments, including survey distribution, response tracking, follow-up with non-respondents, and timely data entry, to ensure complete and usable evaluation data.

Caseload & Match Management (35%)

Match Support
: Manage a caseload of e-matches, providing regular, personalized support to mentors and mentees to help each relationship thrive virtually. This includes conducting regular check-ins with matches to monitor relationship health, celebrate milestones, and identify and address concerns early and guiding matches through intentional match closure/graduation. 
Harm Reduction & Adult-Centered Support
: Provide match support grounded in harm reduction and trauma-informed practice, centering autonomy, informed decision-making, and self-determination given that most e-mentees are legal adults.
Risk Management
: Identify potential risks or liabilities specific to the virtual nature of matches and respond according to SLM policy, escalating to the Senior Director of Programs as needed.
Mentee Engagement Innovation
: Design and implement creative strategies to sustain mentee engagement, including quarterly workshops, compelling rollouts of new resources and opportunities, and persistent, creative follow-up with unresponsive or low-engagement mentees.
Caseload Calibration
: Partner with the Senior Director of Programs to to establish a pathway toward supervising future match support roles in e-mentoring (e.g., track workload and help determine sustainable caseload sizes as the program grows, provide insights for hiring/onboarding new e-mentoring staff, etc.) 

Collaboration & Program Support (25%)

Partnership Support
: Support the identification and maintenance of relationships with strategic partners relevant to the e-mentoring program, in coordination with the Senior Director of Programs and Chief Strategy Officer.
Team Collaboration
: Participate as an active member of the Programs Department, sharing updates and collaborating with other Program Managers on shared practices, tools, and challenges; coordinate with the Volunteer Manager and Enrollment Specialist on mentor recruitment/allocation and mentee recruitment and enrollment specific to e-mentoring.
Cross-Departmental Collaboration
: Participate in relevant working groups to promote cross-departmental collaboration and strategy insight on programming that impacts mentees, mentors, and program staff, including partnering with the Development team to identify and uplift match experiences and stories.
Partner & Donor Reporting
: Compile program reports for partners and donors, pulling and interpreting Salesforce data to present the right metrics, and proactively flagging reportable milestones and trends to the Senior Director of Programs and Development team.
DEI Engagement
: Actively engage in SLM's Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) efforts, such as attending all-staff trainings, providing and receiving feedback, and embracing accountability.
Professionalism & Confidentiality
: Maintain the professional competence and confidentiality necessary to perform job responsibilities.

Our ideal candidate will be a values-led, adaptable individual interested in supporting youth impacted by
foster care. Data shows that BIPOC and women often rule themselves out from job opportunities when
they don’t feel they fit 100% of the criteria listed in a job description. If that sounds like you, don’t rule
yourself out.

3–5 years of experience in program or project management, case management, or direct service work with young adults/transition aged-youth, ideally including experience building or improving a program rather than only running an established one
Master's degree in Social Work (MSW), a comparable degree, OR equivalent work experience that demonstrates skill in providing trauma-informed, harm-reduction, and strengths-based support; LCSW, LICSW, LMHC, or comparable licensure also preferred
Strong commitment to, and belief in, the mission, vision, and values of Silver Lining Mentoring
Sound judgment, especially around participant safety, harm reduction, and organizational liability. This role is expected to grow into a supervisory position over the next 6–12 months, so the ability to make and stand behind good calls independently, and to know when and how to escalate is essential

Seeking Breakthrough Makers

Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) offers countless ways to change lives. Our diverse community of more than 20,000 Breakthrough Makers will inspire you to pursue passions, develop expertise, and drive innovation.

At CHOP, your experience is valued; your voice is heard; and your contributions make a difference for patients and families. Join us as we build on our promise to advance pediatric care—and your career.

CHOP does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, sex, national origin, religion, or any other legally protected categories in any employment, training, or vendor decisions or programs. CHOP recognizes the critical importance of a workforce rich in varied backgrounds and experiences and engages in ongoing efforts to achieve that through equally varied and non-discriminatory means.

A Brief Overview

The Emotion and Neurodiversity Laboratory (ENL) led by Dr. John Herrington at the Center for Autism Research at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia studies the social and emotional experiences of neurodivergent youth. A central component of this position involves working on a new NIH grant focused on the identification facial expressions and other non-verbal behavior that can predict conversational success and satisfaction among autistic and non-autistic adolescents. Working at ENL provides the opportunity to collaborate with a wide range of collaborators to conduct innovative, breakthrough scientific research that improves the lives of stakeholders and families.

We are seeking a full-time Clinical Research Assistant I (CRA I). A 2-year commitment is preferred.

The CRA will organize data processing workflows, monitor undergraduate students, and support clinical study tasks simultaneously.

CRA duties may include but will not be limited to: assisting with study administration, virtual and in-person; maintaining accurate records; organizing data collected through paper or online questionnaires and tests; compiling and processing large quantities of data under the direction of the principal investigator; performing data entry, coding, and analysis; entering testing data into databases and/or spreadsheets; statistical analysis of data using analytical software (e.g., R Studio) and Excel; assisting with IRB protocol amendments, poster presentations, and publication preparation (including conducting literature reviews, creating figures, etc.).

The CRA will work as part of a multi-disciplinary team composed of clinical psychologists, physicians, developmental psychologists, and computer scientists. ENL is a collaborative environment; we are looking for a self-motivated team player with excellent problem-solving and interpersonal skills to support our research efforts.

Under the direct supervision of the Principal Investigator and/or other study team members, this role provides support in the conduct of clinical research.

Job responsibilities may include human subject research activities including but not limited to subject enrollment, data/sample collection, data entry, and regulatory submissions support.

What You Will Do

Provide technical and administrative support in the conduct of clinical research:
Patient/research participant scheduling
Patient/Research Participant screening for inclusion/exclusion criteria or case history
Data collection
Data entry
Data management
Laboratory sample processing
Clinical research study procedures or questionnaire administration
Organization of research records and/or other study related documentation
Research Study Compliance
Adhere to IRB approved protocols and compliance with HIPAA and handling confidential materials
Comply with Institutional policies, SOPs and guidelines
Comply with federal, state, and sponsor policies
Additional Responsibilities may include:
Consent subjects, with appropriate authorization and training
Document and report adverse events
Maintain study source documents
Complete case report forms (paper and electronic data capture)
Assist with IRB/regulatory submissions
Complete case report forms or other study documentation (paper and electronic data capture)
Follow-up care
Order materials/supplies
Schedule research meetings

High School Diploma / GED - Required
Bachelor's Degree - Preferred

Experience Qualifications

Previous relevant clinical research experience - Required
At least one (1) year of relevant clinical research experience - Preferred

Skills And Abilities

Familiarity with IRB and human subject protection.
